question.text: Zenith Private Equity AIF (Cat II) is about to appoint a custodian. The sponsor group owns 30% of Prism Custody Services Ltd. Under SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations, 2024, can Prism Custody Services be appointed as custodian?

answer.text: Yes — related-party custodians are permitted without any conditions for Cat I/II AIFs
Yes — related-party appointment is allowed only if the corpus is below INR 500 crore
No — custodian must always be a public-sector entity like SHCIL
No — the custodian cannot be a related party to the sponsor or designated partners, UNLESS specific conditions prescribed under the 2024 amendment are fulfilled

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations, 2024 (w.e.f. 5-Jan-2024) provide that the custodian SHALL NOT be a related party to the sponsors or designated partners, UNLESS specific conditions (such as arm's-length dealing, independent oversight, robust chinese walls, disclosure to investors) are fulfilled. The chapter explicitly notes this carve-out. The Trap: The 'unconditionally permitted' option ignores the related-party bar. The INR 500 cr option invents a corpus threshold. The public-sector-only option fabricates a rule — multiple private custodians (Deutsche, HSBC, Kotak, SBI-SG) are SEBI-registered. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same rule. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests the LP disclosure obligation when there's a related-party custodian. XXIV (AML) covers the independent-custody principle as an AML safeguard. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even if the 'specific conditions' are satisfiable, LPs (especially institutional FOFs and SWFs) strongly prefer a fully unrelated custodian — don't create a PPM red flag by defaulting to a group custody house unless there's a clear pricing/service benefit.
